name: matlog
description: 📓 A local-only BJJ training journal: one tap to log class, open mat, drilling, comps and rounds; mat hours, sub ratios, a position graph and belt timeline. No account; data stays on your device.

paragraphs: A BJJ training journal that keeps everything on your phone. One tap starts a class, open mat, drilling session, comp or round, and you get clear ways to see your progress: mat hours, a week-by-week heatmap, subs for and against, where you get stuck, your techniques as a position graph, and your belt and stripe timeline.

matlog is a sibling of tinylog and uses the same template: one tap to log, easy to log late, patterns but never advice, and your data stays on your device. It's a static site on GitHub Pages; your log lives in your browser's IndexedDB, with a second copy in localStorage.
features: One tap. Class, Open mat, Drilling, Comp and Round (plus Study, off by default). A tap logs one you just did, with its length and details. Prefer a timer? Turn off log past sessions only in Settings → Buttons, and it's…
Topic. An optional "what the class was about" on any session; when it names a technique, that technique's page lists the sessions on it.

Logging late is normal. Every log shows Undo, −5m / −15m / −30m and Details. With timers on, hold a card to log one you already did, with its length (1 hour for a class by default). Classes start on the hour by default,…

Round log. Stopping a round asks who you rolled with (partner, belt, size), where it started (positional rounds, top or bottom), subs you hit, what you tapped to, moves you landed and moves you went for (sweeps, passes,…

Situational sparring. A round can carry its goal or rules ("bottom escapes or sweeps"), a count of how many times you and your partner each got yours (rounds reset and go again), and a line on how it went. The next…

One tap starts a class, open mat, drilling session, comp or round, and you get clear ways to see your progress: mat hours, a week-by-week heatmap, subs for and against, where you get stuck, your techniques as a position graph, and your belt and stripe timeline.

requirements.text: Open the app → It's free, with no account and no ads, and it works offline.
Where matlog fits: it's for someone who wants a fast, good-looking journal with real stats, without a sign-up, a subscription or a coach in the app.
There are no accounts, servers or analytics, and the only network request is for fonts.
